findings.summary: spawnAgentRunWorker deletes the mandatory --input payload file out from under the live worker. The file is written, passed as `--input <path>`, then removed in a `finally` that runs as soon as spawnWorkerProcess resolves — which for a real long-running agent-run is the SPAWN_READY_GRACE_MS (2000ms) readiness timer, after which the child is unref'd and still running. A real agent-run that has not yet read the payload within that window sees ENOENT on a flag the spec says dispatch.ts:795 hard-requires, yielding exactly the CONTRACT_ERROR failure mode spec §1.1 names. The payload lifetime must be tied to the child's consumption/exit, not to an unrelated readiness timer.

Acceptance P4 is never evaluated on the production default path. P4 requires reading the file that the default argv's `--input` points at and asserting clue_id/clue_text are non-empty, but the composed-default test only asserts the path's filename pattern and tmpdir prefix — it cannot read the file because spawnAgentRunWorker has already deleted it. Payload content is asserted only on a file built directly by writeWorkerInputFile in the P4/P5 unit tests, never on the file actually handed to the spawned agent-run. This is spec §4.1 discipline 8 (an invariant held at one layer is not held at another) applied to the very layer this package exists to close.

Unresolvable agent-run is not loud on the production CLI path. runWrite's dispatch branch swallows every spawn error with a bare `catch`, including AgentRunUnresolvedError, so `tick-entry --run` CASes the card back to open, prints spawned:false and exits 0 with nothing naming agent-run on stderr. Spec §1.4 requires non-zero exit plus naming agent-run; that holds only at the resolveAgentRunBin unit layer. The consequence is also the harm spec §0.1 sets out to eliminate: two irreversible append-only bus writes per open card per tick, silently, forever.

The second spawnWorker dependency surface was not widened. TickDeps.spawnWorker still has the pre-A8d signature (clueId, role, runId?) and runTick's dispatch branch calls it with two arguments, dropping the runId and the newly added decision.text/depth/sources that decideTick now emits. This orchestrator is off the production --run path (tick-entry routes through runChannelWrite), so it is not a blocker, but it is an exported tick orchestrator that silently discards the clue text spec §1.3 requires to be carried through to the worker.
